notes: Every issue of 1967-1969 read through a mention pass: every number followed by a street name in the EAS street list, then a filter dropping other cities, home addresses, advertisements and addresses recurring in six or more issues (advertisers and the masthead); the 256 surviving windows were read by hand. Taken: dated events at buildings, retrospective building histories, and dated occupancy by institutions, associations, churches, clinics, theatres, schools and firms. Not taken: display and classified advertising, home addresses of private people, crime reports at homes, and out-of-city pages.

coverage.remaining: 1970 onward is a separate batch; see the dossier. Advertisements in these issues were not extracted.
coverage.note: 2045 numbered-address mentions in 136 issues; 256 survived the filter and were read; 51 findings.

citation.label: East/West: The Chinese-American Journal, vol. 3, no. 18 (30 April 1969), p. 7

raw.text: 17 Adler Place (off 1140 Grant Ave.) at the headquarters building of the Chinese Historical Society of America

resolution.method: sf-eas-addresses holds no street named ADLER PL, under that spelling or any spelling of it, so the address cannot be looked up. The archivist's second address ("1140 Grant Ave.") has no EAS record either.
resolution.note: The street the record names is not a street in the city's address registry today; the record may name a private way, a renamed street or a spelling this pass could not match.

findings.description: Chinese Hospital's newly opened out-patient department was here, behind the hospital.

citation.label: East/West: The Chinese-American Journal, vol. 3, no. 25 (18 June 1969), p. 5

raw.text: the newly opened out-patient department behind the hospital at 40 Trenton Street

resolution.method: No record in sf-eas-addresses for 40 TRENTON ST.
resolution.note: The address does not exist today, so there is no page it can go on. The nearest surviving numbers on the street are 20, 50. Per "The evidence bar" in research/AGENTS.md this is a street-hub fact: a dated record of a building at a number the city no longer has.

findings.description: The housing committee of the San Francisco Planning and Urban Renewal Association resolved to oppose demolition of the International Hotel, asking that it be kept as a community centre and housing for its Filipino tenants.

citation.label: East/West: The Chinese-American Journal, vol. 3, no. 25 (18 June 1969), p. 5

raw.text: opposing demolition of the International Hotel ... retention of the hotel situated at 848 Kearny Street

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 848 KEARNY ST → parcel 0195021; sf-parcels has blklot 0195021 active, 848–868 KEARNY; the 2025 roll records it as multi-family residential, built 2005. EAS puts 848, 868 KEARNY ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 848.

findings.description: The National Dollar Store's garment factory here, the largest in Chinatown, was struck by the Chinese Ladies' Garment Workers, a local of the International Ladies Garment Workers Union. The factory closed rather than meet the union's demands.

findings.description: Golden Gate Church was here and started a Saturday-morning Chinese class in February 1969.

citation.label: East/West: The Chinese-American Journal, vol. 3, no. 7 (12 February 1969), p. 5

raw.text: New Sat. morning Chinese class at Golden Gate Church 829 25th Ave.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 829 25TH AVE → parcel 1668046; sf-parcels has blklot 1668046 active, 829–829 25TH; the 2025 roll records it as single family residential, built 1930. Parcel 1668046 is one unit of a condominium (the 2025 roll classes this parcel as a Condominium with zero lot area, which is a unit and not a building); the fact is the building's, and goes on the building's page at this path, which lists its units (#228).
resolution.note: No page at this path yet; the publisher seeds it with seed-list, which writes a condominium building with a page per unit.
